Missouri false-impersonation correction filing guide

Stop this self-help route and seek legal assistance if any of these conditions applies: The impersonator is a family member, a
former partner or someone else known to the participant, which changes both the available evidence and what the
participant should do next.; A conviction was entered under the participant's identity, particularly where a sentence was
served or supervision imposed.; The participant has been arrested, detained or denied employment, housing or a licence
because of the false record.; The prosecuting attorney or a named agency disputes the account, or the court sets a
contested hearing.; The participant is unsure whether their situation is false impersonation under § 575.120 or mistaken
identity under § 610.145, because the two run in different courts on different forms.; The record appears on a private
background check after the court order, which a Missouri court order does not reach.; The participant is contemplating a civil
claim against the impersonator or against an agency.; There are false records in more than one Missouri county, or in another
state.; The participant is not a United States citizen or there is any immigration consequence.; The participant cannot obtain
fingerprint cards from any local agency.

If you reported identity theft or are advised to do so, obtain the police report and FTC identity-theft report at identitytheft.gov.
These can corroborate the record; neither is required by section 575.120.4. A Missouri court order does not itself reach
credit-bureau records.

Prepared for Jordan Lee Example. Synthetic review fixture only.

This is correction of records caused by false impersonation under section 575.120.4, using the civil procedure in section
610.123. Someone else was arrested or convicted under your identity. It does not erase that person's actual offense; it
expunges your falsely ascribed identifying factors and corrects the record. It is different from CR301 mistaken identity after
dismissal/acquittal and from general section 610.140 expungement.

File the verified CR300 petition and standard fingerprint card with the civil division of the circuit court in Jackson County,
where the arrest occurred. Confirm current clerk address, filing method, required copies, confidential filing sheet and whether
CR310 is requested. The clerk assigns the new civil case number; the underlying criminal case belongs in CR300's record
row.

Obtain the arrest report and certified docket/judgment showing exactly which identifying factors were falsely used. Order your
fingerprint-based Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal-history record through its CJIS Division / Missouri Automated
Criminal History Site and compare it with the name-based false record. Confirm Patrol search fees first. Compare your full
name, sex, race, birth date, Social Security number, driver's license number, address at arrest, charged offense, arrest date,
arrest county/municipality, arresting agency, and underlying case/court division. The verified petition must supply mandatory
section 610.123 contents; missing contents can require dismissal. Do not guess an unknown citation, conviction date or
perpetrator identity.

Document the substantial number of your identifying factors falsely attributed to the person actually arrested or convicted. No
waiting period, acquittal/dismissal, no-conviction condition or general expungement lifetime limit is imposed by this route.
Disputed impersonation or insufficient identity evidence requires legal help; this packet does not establish the court's finding.

Arrange three standard fingerprint cards from a local police or sheriff agency. Ask whether it takes applicant prints, can
supply three cards in one visit, its cost, payment method and required identification. One card goes to the court, one is sent
by the clerk to the Missouri Criminal Record Repository and one is yours to keep. These are external: obtain real fingerprints
and submit the required card with the petition for identity verification. No fingerprint card, fingerprints or officer signature is
manufactured. The clerk forwards the petition and card to the Missouri Criminal Record Repository.

Name every official, agency or entity holding the affected records, with complete service address. The order reaches named
entities. The attached respondent schedule preserves the complete supplied list. Confirm additional record holders before
signing; do not omit one to fit a form.

Missouri false-impersonation correction filing guide

The clerk issues a petition copy to each named entity and gives the prosecutor and each named entity hearing notice. The
court sets a hearing no sooner than 30 days after filing, with reasonable notice; no hearing date or completed service is
supplied here. Seek legal help for objections, disputed facts or a hearing.

Confirm ordinary civil filing/service costs with the clerk; no universal local total is established here. GN10 is offered as an
option because this route has no statutory fee exemption. If unable to pay, request GN10 and complete current income,
expenses, assets and debts, including spouse finances when married. Sign personally after review; a submitted waiver
request is not approval. This route is not the section 610.140 surcharge route.

Review and personally sign the CR300 perjury declaration. CR300 prescribes no notarial acknowledgment; do not import the
CR145 notarization requirement. Keep Social Security numbers and financial information in the court-required confidential
process; FI-05 is confidential. FI-05 uses the held source code table: XG, Expungement of Crim/Arrest Record, with PET for
petitioner and RES for respondents. Ask the clerk about protected-document procedures. GN10 appears only when
requested; CR310 only when the clerk expects a proposed order; FI-05 when opening a new case or required by the clerk.

CR310 is an unsigned proposed judicial instrument. Leave judicial findings/directions, judgment date and signature to the
court; no result is promised. After entry, obtain the signed order, confirm clerk copies went to every named record holder and
compare corrected court/repository records. Section 610.124 provides repository follow-through including its FBI request; do
not assume all federal or private copies are corrected automatically. If a named record remains wrong, contact the
clerk/agency with the entered order and seek counsel as needed.

Missouri false-impersonation correction filing guide

Stop this self-help route and seek legal assistance if any of these conditions applies: The impersonator is a family member, a
former partner or someone else known to the participant, which changes both the available evidence and what the
participant should do next.; A conviction was entered under the participant's identity, particularly where a sentence was
served or supervision imposed.; The participant has been arrested, detained or denied employment, housing or a licence
because of the false record.; The prosecuting attorney or a named agency disputes the account, or the court sets a
contested hearing.; The participant is unsure whether their situation is false impersonation under § 575.120 or mistaken
identity under § 610.145, because the two run in different courts on different forms.; The record appears on a private
background check after the court order, which a Missouri court order does not reach.; The participant is contemplating a civil
claim against the impersonator or against an agency.; There are false records in more than one Missouri county, or in another
state.; The participant is not a United States citizen or there is any immigration consequence.; The participant cannot obtain
fingerprint cards from any local agency.

If you reported identity theft or are advised to do so, obtain the police report and FTC identity-theft report at identitytheft.gov.
These can corroborate the record; neither is required by section 575.120.4. A Missouri court order does not itself reach
credit-bureau records.

This is correction of records caused by false impersonation under section 575.120.4, using the civil procedure in section
610.123. Someone else was arrested or convicted under your identity. It does not erase that person's actual offense; it
expunges your falsely ascribed identifying factors and corrects the record. It is different from CR301 mistaken identity after
dismissal/acquittal and from general section 610.140 expungement.

File the verified CR300 petition and standard fingerprint card with the civil division of the circuit court in Jackson County,
where the arrest occurred. Confirm current clerk address, filing method, required copies, confidential filing sheet and whether
CR310 is requested. The clerk assigns the new civil case number; the underlying criminal case belongs in CR300's record
row.

Obtain the arrest report and certified docket/judgment showing exactly which identifying factors were falsely used. Order your
fingerprint-based Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal-history record through its CJIS Division / Missouri Automated
Criminal History Site and compare it with the name-based false record. Confirm Patrol search fees first. Compare your full
name, sex, race, birth date, Social Security number, driver's license number, address at arrest, charged offense, arrest date,
arrest county/municipality, arresting agency, and underlying case/court division. The verified petition must supply mandatory
section 610.123 contents; missing contents can require dismissal. Do not guess an unknown citation, conviction date or
perpetrator identity.

Document the substantial number of your identifying factors falsely attributed to the person actually arrested or convicted. No
waiting period, acquittal/dismissal, no-conviction condition or general expungement lifetime limit is imposed by this route.
Disputed impersonation or insufficient identity evidence requires legal help; this packet does not establish the court's finding.

Arrange three standard fingerprint cards from a local police or sheriff agency. Ask whether it takes applicant prints, can
supply three cards in one visit, its cost, payment method and required identification. One card goes to the court, one is sent
by the clerk to the Missouri Criminal Record Repository and one is yours to keep. These are external: obtain real fingerprints
and submit the required card with the petition for identity verification. No fingerprint card, fingerprints or officer signature is
manufactured. The clerk forwards the petition and card to the Missouri Criminal Record Repository.

Name every official, agency or entity holding the affected records, with complete service address. The order reaches named
entities. The attached respondent schedule preserves the complete supplied list. Confirm additional record holders before
signing; do not omit one to fit a form.

contract.legalName: Petition for Correction of Arrest/Court Records on False Impersonation (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 575.120.4, procedure under § 610.123)
contract.publicName: Correcting a record created by identity theft
contract.mechanism: The review recorded the statutory basis and scope of CR300 as not established and made it the track's build blocker. It is now established, from the official form's own face and from the statute it cites. CR300 states: Pursuant to sections 575.120.4 and 610.123, RSMo, I hereby request that the court issue an order to expunge the following arrest and court records that falsely identify me and to correct the arrest and court records to accurately reflect the identity of the defendant. Its footer carries the same two citations. § 575.120 is the false impersonation offense, and subsection 4 supplies the victim's civil remedy: any person who is the victim of a false impersonation and whose identity has been falsely reported in arrest or conviction records may move for expungement and correction of those records under the procedures set forth in § 610.123, and upon a showing that a substantial number of identifying factors of the victim was falsely ascribed to the person actually arrested or convicted, the court shall order the false identifying factors contained in the arrest and court records amended to correctly and accurately identify the defendant and shall expunge the incorrect and inaccurate factors from the arrest and court records. That single provision answers every question the review left open. The relief is correction plus targeted expungement of the false identifying factors, not expungement of the case. The proof is a substantial number of identifying factors falsely ascribed, which is a different and in some ways lower showing than § 610.145's identity-used-without-permission finding. Relief is mandatory on that showing: the court shall order. The procedure is § 610.123's, which means a verified petition in the civil division of the circuit court in the county of the arrest, the eleven mandatory contents whose absence requires dismissal, the standard fingerprint card filed with the petition and forwarded to the central repository, defendants named with the order reaching only those named, and a hearing set no sooner than thirty days from filing with reasonable notice to each named entity. And critically the section reaches arrest or conviction records: unlike § 610.145 it does not require that the charge against the participant was dismissed or that they were acquitted, because the point is that somebody else was arrested or convicted under the participant's identity. The adopted Batch 2 memorandum's direction to keep this route separate from CR301 is therefore not merely preserved but strengthened: they are different statutes, different courts, different divisions, different proof and different remedies. The memorandum's primary-authority line cites § 610.145 for both forms; the form's own citation controls and is recorded as a correction.

packetInstructions: This route corrects a record so that it identifies the person actually arrested or convicted, and expunges the incorrect and inaccurate identifying factors. It does not make the case disappear. The packet says so plainly, because a participant told their record will be expunged and then shown the case still existing under someone else's name will reasonably feel misled.

This track is kept separate from the § 610.145 mistaken-identity route and the two are never substituted for one another. Different statute, different court, different division, different proof, different remedy — and only this one is available where a conviction was entered under the participant's identity.

Filing is in the civil division of the circuit court in the county of arrest, which CR300 recites on its face. A participant who takes this to the court where the case was heard, as they would for a mistaken-identity petition, will be in the wrong place.

A Missouri court order does not reach a private background-check database or a credit file. The packet routes the participant to the ordinary consumer identity-theft remedies alongside the court filing and says plainly that they are different problems with different fixes.

The full Social Security number goes on the face of CR300 because § 610.123.1(1)(f) makes it a mandatory content whose absence requires dismissal, and the impersonator's identifying details may appear too where the participant knows them. The confidentiality of the filing therefore matters more on this route than anywhere else in the Missouri set, and the packet says so.

The standard fingerprint card is a mandatory content of the petition under § 610.123.1(7) and is obtained before filing from a local law enforcement agency. On this route it is also the participant's best evidence, because a fingerprint is the one identifier an impersonator cannot borrow. It never delays generation.
scopeRestrictions: Offered only where the participant reports that another person's arrest or conviction was recorded under their identity. Where the participant was themselves named because a witness or officer misidentified them and the charge was dismissed or they were acquitted, the route is § 610.145 on CR301.

selfHelpStopConditions: The impersonator is a family member, a former partner or someone else known to the participant, which changes both the available evidence and what the participant should do next.
A conviction was entered under the participant's identity, particularly where a sentence was served or supervision imposed.
The participant has been arrested, detained or denied employment, housing or a licence because of the false record.
The prosecuting attorney or a named agency disputes the account, or the court sets a contested hearing.
The participant is unsure whether their situation is false impersonation under § 575.120 or mistaken identity under § 610.145, because the two run in different courts on different forms.
The record appears on a private background check after the court order, which a Missouri court order does not reach.
The participant is contemplating a civil claim against the impersonator or against an agency.
There are false records in more than one Missouri county, or in another state.
The participant is not a United States citizen or there is any immigration consequence.
The participant cannot obtain fingerprint cards from any local agency.

unresolvedQuestions.question: Whether § 610.124's destruction regime applies to a correction ordered under § 575.120.4. § 575.120.4 borrows the procedures set forth in § 610.123, and § 610.124 by its terms governs all records ordered to be expunged pursuant to § 610.123. On that reading the false identifying factors would be destroyed or blacked out and removed from Missouri electronic files, with the central repository requesting Federal Bureau of Investigation expungement. That is a strong reading with real participant consequences and the packet does not assert it: it says the false factors are corrected and expunged, and does not promise destruction.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: This route corrects a record so that it identifies the person actually arrested or convicted, and expunges the incorrect and inaccurate identifying factors. It does not make the case disappear. The packet says so plainly, because a participant told their record will be expunged and then shown the case still existing under someone else's name will reasonably feel misled.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: This track is kept separate from the § 610.145 mistaken-identity route and the two are never substituted for one another. Different statute, different court, different division, different proof, different remedy — and only this one is available where a conviction was entered under the participant's identity.

provenance.sourceStatement: It is distinct from CR301, which addresses mistaken identity. Keep the two routes separate, use the form matching the factual mechanism, and do not substitute a general § 610.140 expungement petition.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Filing is in the civil division of the circuit court in the county of arrest, which CR300 recites on its face. A participant who takes this to the court where the case was heard, as they would for a mistaken-identity petition, will be in the wrong place.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: A Missouri court order does not reach a private background-check database or a credit file. The packet routes the participant to the ordinary consumer identity-theft remedies alongside the court filing and says plainly that they are different problems with different fixes.

provenance.sourceHeading: Packet identity versus commercial scope
provenance.sourceStatement: For Maryland Track 10, Georgia Track M, Michigan Track 5, and similar specialized routes, store packet identity and product enablement as separate fields.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: The standard fingerprint card is a mandatory content of the petition under § 610.123.1(7) and is obtained before filing from a local law enforcement agency. On this route it is also the participant's best evidence, because a fingerprint is the one identifier an impersonator cannot borrow. It never delays generation.

provenance.sourceHeading: Packet generation is not conditioned on third-party records
provenance.sourceStatement: A criminal-history report, certified disposition, fingerprint card, prosecutor response, court certification, or agency approval is ordinarily a required-before-filing item or later process step. It is not a reason to suppress a paid packet.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: The full Social Security number goes on the face of CR300 because § 610.123.1(1)(f) makes it a mandatory content whose absence requires dismissal, and the impersonator's identifying details may appear too where the participant knows them. The confidentiality of the filing therefore matters more on this route than anywhere else in the Missouri set, and the packet says so.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: The false-impersonation recital, the impersonator's details where unknown, the sworn statement and signature, the case number, the Court ORI and Offense Cycle numbers, the FI-05 case type code and the judge's blocks on CR310 are all left blank.

provenance.sourceHeading: Third-party blocks remain blank
provenance.sourceStatement: Judge, clerk, prosecutor, process-server, notary, law-enforcement, and agency blocks must remain blank unless the form expressly assigns the field to the participant.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Offered only where the participant reports that another person's arrest or conviction was recorded under their identity. Where the participant was themselves named because a witness or officer misidentified them and the charge was dismissed or they were acquitted, the route is § 610.145 on CR301.

provenance.sourceStatement: Why it is listed separately from Track 7: the internal reference treats identity theft and mistaken identity as distinct routes with distinct forms, and OSCA maintains two forms.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Whether a substantial number of the participant's identifying factors was falsely ascribed is the court's finding and LegalEase never asserts it. Where the impersonator is known to the participant, or where a conviction and sentence were entered, the packet refers out before it is generated.

provenance.sourceHeading: Participant facts may be captured; legal advocacy may not be invented
provenance.sourceStatement: LegalEase may ask for and format the participant's own facts. It may not create an interests-of-justice argument, rehabilitation claim, trafficking nexus, public-safety analysis, constitutional claim, or other case-specific legal conclusion.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: A hearing is required and is not a reason to withhold the packet. Self-help ends if the prosecuting attorney or a named agency disputes the account, or the court sets a contested hearing.

provenance.sourceHeading: Scope restrictions and handoffs do not erase packet identity
provenance.sourceStatement: An active sentence, required hearing, discretionary standard, evidentiary burden, local filing practice, or likely objection is represented as a scope restriction, packet instruction, or handoff condition.
